title: The Vow of Rosewater Lane
premise: Tamsin Almeida, a ghostwriter who has built a career on other people's truths, is hired through an anonymous literary exchange to correspond with a fellow writer during the coastal town of Bellhaven's month-long Rosewater Festival. The letters turn intimate — until she discovers her pen pal is Julian Ashe, the rival memoirist she is secretly ghostwriting for, and that the letters were paired deliberately by his estranged sister, who believes Julian buried the truth about the fire that killed their father. As Tamsin pieces together the real story from drafts, letters, and lies, she must choose between the loyalty her contract demands and the truth the Ashe family deserves, confessing her double role at the festival's closing night. Julian's fury gives way to a reckoning with his own memory, and the two publish the corrected memoir together — signing it, at last, with both their names.
about_author: D. M. Vane is the pen name of a former court stenographer who spent fifteen years transcribing other people's confessions before writing her own. She lives in a converted lighthouse keeper's cottage on the northern coast, where she still answers every letter by hand.

chapters.title: The Ghost's Contract
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She signs a lucrative, ironclad NDA to ghostwrite Julian Ashe's memoir, telling herself the heart is a muscle she can train to stay flat. Emotional beat: controlled cynicism masking a old wound from a love she once ghosted out of.

chapters.title: Rosewater, Anonymous
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Bellhaven literary society's pen-pal festival assigns her a correspondent — first letter arrives unsigned, warm, disarmingly honest. She answers with a borrowed voice, then, startled, with her own. Beat: cautious curiosity.

chapters.title: The Man Who Writes Himself
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian begins the exchange as a publicity stunt, dictating charm, then finds himself writing things his memoir won't admit. Beat: the crack in the performance.

chapters.title: Drafts and Ashes
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Working through Julian's manuscript, she finds a gap where Chapter Nine should be — the fire, the father, the missing year. The anonymous letters begin echoing the gaps. Beat: unease sharpening into suspicion.

chapters.title: What the Tide Keeps
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Festival errands take her to Bellhaven's shoreline; she meets Priya Ashe, Julian's estranged sister, who recognizes her brother's phrasing in a letter Tamsin quotes. Beat: the first thread pulled loose.

chapters.title: Two Inboxes
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian realizes he's falling for a stranger on paper while bristling at his ghostwriter's questions in person — questions that sound uncannily like his pen pal's. Beat: dramatic irony tightening.

chapters.title: The Chapter That Isn't There
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Priya reveals her theory: their father's death was no accident, and Julian rewrote the night to protect someone. Tamsin, sworn to loyalty, starts investigating anyway. Beat: loyalty and truth begin to pull apart.

chapters.title: Letters at Low Water
chapters.summary: Dual letters, both POVs. The pen-pal exchange turns confessional — first love, first betrayal — each writing truths they can't say aloud to anyone they can see. Beat: intimacy without faces.

chapters.title: The Neighbor's Testimony
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. A retired harbormaster remembers the fire differently than the memoir does: someone left the boathouse before it burned, and Julian's account protects that someone. Beat: the mystery gains a shape.

chapters.title: Ink Under the Fingernails
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian catches his ghostwriter with his sister and assumes a betrayal — a leak, a rival bid. He drafts a cruel letter to his pen pal, then can't send it. Beat: jealousy misreading itself.

chapters.title: The Festival of Small Fires
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Mid-festival lantern night; Tamsin and Julian share a dance that neither will name, both half in love with the person behind the other's mask. Beat: the heart refusing containment.

chapters.title: Chapter Nine, Restored
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. In Julian's early drafts she finds the original Chapter Nine — his father alive at midnight, an argument, a promise broken. The fire was cover for a debt, and Julian took the blame in print. Beat: the truth arrives, unwelcome.

chapters.title: The Pairing
chapters.summary: Priya's POV. Priya confesses she rigged the pen-pal pairing, betting the right stranger could get Julian honest. Tamsin realizes she was a tool in someone else's justice. Beat: fury and recognition — she has done the same to readers for years.

chapters.title: What the Contract Gags
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Julian's publisher threatens legal ruin if the fire chapter changes; Tamsin's own career hangs on her silence. She drafts the honest chapter anyway, alone, at 3 a.m. Beat: the vow she never made, made.

chapters.title: A Letter Returned Unopened
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian discovers the handwriting — his pen pal and his ghostwriter are one woman. He reads every letter again in a single night, rewriting his whole understanding of her. Beat: betrayal braided with tenderness.

chapters.title: Confrontation at the Boathouse
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian confronts Tamsin at the ruined boathouse; the argument strips both masks off — the ghost, the liar, the grieving son. He walks away. Beat: the midpoint wound, deepest cut.

chapters.title: The Harbormaster's Ledger
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The harbormaster's old ledger proves who actually set the fire: the family's trusted business partner, now a festival patron. Justice outside the law — the statute long expired. Beat: the truth needs a witness, not a verdict.

chapters.title: Reading the Evidence Aloud
chapters.summary: Tamsin and Priya, alternating. They assemble the case: ledger, draft, testimony. Tamsin argues for publication, not prosecution — let the record be the punishment. Beat: purpose replacing heartbreak.

chapters.title: Closing Night
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. At the festival's final reading, Tamsin takes the stage, confesses her double role to the town and to Julian, and reads the restored Chapter Nine aloud. Beat: the climax — truth as an act of love, whatever it costs.

chapters.title: The Silence After Applause
chapters.summary: Julian's POV. Julian, publicly unmasked and privately freed, walks out — then returns to the empty stage and finishes the chapter in his own voice, naming his father's killer and his own cowardice. Beat: reckoning, and the first honest word between them.

chapters.title: Bylines
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Winter in Bellhaven. The corrected memoir publishes under both names — ghost and author side by side. Julian asks her to write with him, not for him. Beat: the whole heart, risked and returned.

chapters.title: The Vow of Rosewater Lane
chapters.summary: Both POVs, interleaved letters. On the anniversary of the festival, they exchange one last anonymous letter each — then sign their names for the first time. Beat: resolution; memory kept honest, loyalty and truth reconciled in ink.
